title: perimeter-health-integration-scribe
body:
Context: quick capture after 9/17 customer call with Perimeter Health (PH). Theyre evaluating Redwood Private for an on-prem inference gateway to serve clinical triage assistant. Key: PH is very sensitive about PHI, strict network segmentation, and auditability. They want a short POC (2-3 weeks) proving low-latency triage responses under typical hospital network constraints and an exportable audit trail for each request.

Call attendees: PH - Dinesh Patel (CTO), Maya Lin (Sr. Sys Architect), Laura Choi (Compliance); Redwood - Priya (SE), Evan (Infra), Jorge (PM).

High-level ask / success metrics (from PH):
- 95th pct latency under 220ms for 256-token responses with 3 concurrent clinician sessions (burst to 12).
- End-to-end audit log of prompts + model outputs with tamper-evident signature and retention for 7 years (compliance requirement).
- No egress of raw patient identifiers beyond customer VPC; any telemetry must be opt-in and filtered.
- Can failover to cloud-hosted Redwood Dedicated in >30s for disaster recovery.
- Demonstrate RBAC for model versions and staff-level access controls.

Architecture notes they prefer:
- On-prem control plane (air-gapped is not required initially, but must be supported later).
- Model weights inside PH environment (they will host model bundle on their storage).
- Private KMS integration (HSM + customer keys) for envelope encryption of logs and model artifacts.
- Preferred infra: 2 x A100-equivalent nodes behind a north-south LB inside their PCI/HIPAA zone; option to scale to GPU++ if needed.

Technical constraints / gotchas raised by PH: (note these may affect POC scope)
1) MTU & network policy: Their EMR network enforces MTU=1400 and has strict egress proxies. We need to validate TLS/keepalive behavior with smaller packets and the runtime's long-lived KV cache connections.
2) K8s CNI: They run Calico with eBPF and strict network policies; our sidecar or control-plane agents must not assume hostNetwork access.
3) Proxying SNI: their outbound gateway terminates SNI for external endpoints; our fallback to Redwood Dedicated must support SNI passthrough or we need to route via an approved jump host.
4) GPU scheduler pre-emption: their infra team is worried about node churn during nightly batch jobs; propose node isolation / taints for inference pools.
5) Audit log format: compliance wants chained signatures plus per-request hashes stored in an immutable blob store. They asked if Redwood can emit logs in WORM-ready format (S3 Object Lock or equivalent).
6) Latency test realism: baseline EMR traffic includes occasional <50ms jitter spikes; need to reproduce in POC using their traffic replay capture.

POC scope (proposed, keep tight):
- Week 0: Kickoff + infra checklist (network, KMS creds, storage endpoint, approved IP allowlist). Define acceptance criteria and test plan.
- Week 1: Deploy Private control plane in PH test VPC (non-airgapped) with 2-node inference pool; load model bundle (customer-provided). Smoke tests: model load, basic generation, audit log emission.
- Week 2: Run replayed clinician traffic at 3 concurrent sessions, validate 95th pct latency and throughput; exercise failover to Redwood Dedicated (controlled trigger).
- Week 3: Compliance handoff: show audit log integrity proof, RBAC demonstration, deliver runbook and hardening notes.

Acceptance criteria (customer-facing):
- 95th pct response latency <220ms for 256-token responses under defined traffic profile.
- Audit logs written to PH-managed bucket with chained signature present and verification script provided.
- No detected egress of raw patient identifiers to Redwood-hosted telemetry endpoints (we will run dataflow check).
- Successful failover test to Redwood Dedicated with <30s RTO in simulated node loss.

Immediate engineering notes / implementation items for Redwood team: 
- Need a small patch to the private-agent to respect HTTP keepalive window when MTU <1500; Evan to prototype. (Action: Evan)
- Implement an option to sign audit log batches with customer-provided HSM keys (envelope: logBatch -> hash -> HSM-sign -> store). Jorge to scope with infra. (Action: Jorge)
- Add an RBAC role demo in console for per-route model pinning and a short screencast. Priya to make playbook. (Action: Priya)
- Create a trimmed traffic-replay harness that can inject PH-specific jitter patterns (open-source style, but config files kept in PH repo). (Action: Evan + PH ops)

Open questions to resolve with PH (to capture in follow-up email):
- They asked about exact format of audit log JSON schema and whether we can append per-request cryptographic proof; provide sample schema.
- Clarify whether model telemetry (perf counters, OOM events) can be redacted and pushed to Redwood telemetry; PH prefers all telemetry disabled by default.
- Confirm allowed outbound IPs and whether a jump-host for Dedicated fallback is acceptable.
- Which HSM vendor/version they plan to use (YubiHSM vs AWS CloudHSM vs Thales).

Risks / blockers:
- If PH insists on air-gapped control plane for POC, time and cost double; raise to sales for SOW amendment.
- Our current audit-signing implementation assumes server-side private key; supporting customer HSM will require infra changes and key lifecycle docs.
- Latency goal aggressive given their network jitter; POC must include synthetic jitter analysis and possibly tune model variants / quantization.

Next steps (short-term checklist):
- Today: send recap email with meeting notes, preliminary POC timeline, and list of infra artifacts we need. (Priya)
- By 9/20: PH to share replay capture (pcap or request traces), KMS contact, and approved IP allowlist.
- By 9/22: Evan to drop a lightweight MTU/keepalive probe script and initial results to the slack thread.
- By 9/24: Jorge to propose PRD for HSM-backed audit signing and rough engineering estimate.
- Schedule: book mid-POC sync on 9/29 to review latency numbers and decide on possible model quantization.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep POC scope tight; do NOT commit to long-term air-gapped/full-onprem without sales SOW.
- Use model variant with 8-bit quantization only if latency tests show it preserves QA measures; coordinate with research for quick eval harness.
- Prepare a short compliance pack: sample audit log + verification script + retention policy doc.

Attachments referenced: PH replay capture (pending), PH security checklist (sent by Laura 9/17), internal slide: Perimeter Health POC one-pager (PR on GH pending).

Raw snippets to include in follow-up email: 
- "We will not enable automatic telemetry export during POC; PH retains full control over telemetry opt-in. Audit logs are written to your S3 endpoint and signed with your HSM-provided key. We propose a 3-week POC focused strictly on latency, failover, and audit integrity. Air-gapped control plane support is planned but out-of-scope for this initial POC and will require an expanded SOW."

End of capture. Will convert to cleaned customer recap and send within 24h.
